package_info.why_malicious: The injected code on the LCBO checkout page was designed to steal customers’ payment information, constituting a classic web skimmer (Magecart-style) attack. This is a direct violation of user trust and site integrity, with the explicit goal of exfiltrating sensitive financial data.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user visits checkout page and enters payment info)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the checkout page JavaScript (likely inline or via a loaded script)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects payment form data from the checkout page, serializes it, and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in payment data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating payment data from a checkout page is a hallmark of web skimming attacks and is never legitimate on a payment page.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal checkout page scripts should only process and transmit payment data to trusted payment processors, not to unknown external domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment processing scripts may collect form data, but only transmit it to trusted, whitelisted domains.
key_indicators: Collection of sensitive payment form fields
Network requests to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains
Code injected into a sensitive payment workflow

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to LCBO website and injects malicious JavaScript into the checkout page.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code in customer browsers

attack_chain.action: Injected script executes in the context of the checkout page, capturing payment information as users enter it.
Captured payment data is sent to an attacker-controlled server via HTTPS POST.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code on payment pages collecting form data and sending it to external domains
Unexpected network requests from checkout pages to non-whitelisted endpoints
Inline or dynamically loaded scripts not present in the legitimate site codebase
file_indicators: Injected or modified JavaScript on checkout/payment pages
References to external scripts or endpoints not used by the legitimate site
network_indicators: POST requests from checkout pages to unknown or suspicious domains
Unusual traffic patterns from payment pages to external IPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript on payment or checkout pages that collects sensitive form data and initiates network requests to domains not associated with the legitimate payment processor. Use content integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized script changes, and inspect outgoing network traffic from sensitive pages for connections to untrusted endpoints.
